info.name: KoboMarket API
info.description: Generated from the OpenAPI spec (npm run postman). Start with Auth -> register, verify, login (the login request stores {{token}}). Money is integer kobo. Every state-changing money request has an Idempotency-Key header filled with {{$guid}}.

item.name: Products
GET /products - Search and list products (public)

request.description:
Full-text search on name and description, filters, sorting and **cursor** pagination.
Pass the returned `nextCursor` back as `cursor` (with the same `sort`) to get the next page.
Money is integer kobo.

item.name: POST /products - Create a product (approved vendors only)

exec: try { const v = j.data.product.id; if (v) pm.collectionVariables.set('productId', v); } catch (e) {}

request.description:
Without variants send `priceKobo` (and `stock`). With variants, each variant has its own
`priceKobo` and `stock`; the product price becomes the lowest variant price and the
stock the total. The slug is generated from the name.

item.name: GET /products/{slug} - Product page by slug (public; inactive or deleted products are 404)

request.description: Product page by slug (public; inactive or deleted products are 404)

item.name: PATCH /products/{id} - Update my product (vendor who owns it)

request.description: Send only the fields to change. `variants` replaces the whole list; keep a variant by sending its `id`.

item.name: DELETE /products/{id} - Soft-delete my product (vendor who owns it)

request.description: Soft-delete my product (vendor who owns it)

item.name: Cart
GET /cart - My cart, priced at CURRENT prices with stock warnings

request.description:
Each item shows the price when it was added (`addedPriceKobo`), the current price,
`priceChanged`, and `issue` (PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE, VARIANT_UNAVAILABLE, OUT_OF_STOCK,
INSUFFICIENT_STOCK) when it cannot be bought as it is. `vendors` groups the purchasable
items by vendor; `totalKobo` counts purchasable items only.

item.name: POST /cart/items - Add a product (or variant) to the cart

request.description: Adding something already in the cart increases its quantity. The total is checked against stock.

item.name: PATCH /cart/items/{itemId} - Set the quantity of a cart item

request.description: Set the quantity of a cart item

item.name: POST /wallet/fund - Start a wallet top-up (returns a checkout URL; no money moves yet)

exec: try { const v = j.data.payment.reference; if (v) pm.collectionVariables.set('reference', v); } catch (e) {}

header.description: New value per logical request; reuse it to see the replay.

request.description:
Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. The same key with the same body returns the original
response; the same key with a different body is 409. The wallet is credited only after the
provider confirms the payment (webhook) and we re-verify it.

item.name: GET /wallet/fund/{reference} - Status of one of my top-ups (also the Paystack callback URL)

request.description: If the payment is still PENDING this asks the provider and credits the wallet if it was paid (a fallback for a missed webhook). Crediting is idempotent.

item.name: Orders
POST /orders/checkout - Check out my cart (pays from my wallet into escrow)

exec: try { const v = j.data.order.subOrders[0].id; if (v) pm.collectionVariables.set('subOrderId', v); } catch (e) {}

header.description: New value per logical request; reuse it to see the replay.

request.description:
Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key never creates two orders (replay returns
the original response). The cart is re-validated against current stock and prices. In one
PostgreSQL transaction the order is created (one parent order, one sub-order per vendor)
and the buyer's wallet is debited into PLATFORM_ESCROW. Stock is then decremented in
MongoDB; if that fails the payment is reversed and the order cancelled.

item.name: GET /orders - My orders, newest first (cursor pagination)

request.description: My orders, newest first (cursor pagination)

item.name: GET /orders/{id} - One order with its sub-orders and items (the buyer, or an admin)

request.description: One order with its sub-orders and items (the buyer, or an admin)

GET /orders/sales - My sales as a vendor (sub-orders), newest first

request.description: My sales as a vendor (sub-orders), newest first

item.name: POST /orders/sub-orders/{id}/ship - Vendor marks a PAID sub-order as SHIPPED

request.description: Only the vendor who owns the sub-order (others get 404). Starts the buyer's 72-hour confirmation window.

item.name: POST /orders/sub-orders/{id}/confirm-delivery - Buyer confirms delivery; the sub-order completes and escrow is released

request.description:
SHIPPED -> DELIVERED -> COMPLETED in one transaction. One ledger transaction moves the
escrow: subtotal minus commission to the vendor's wallet, the commission (the rate
recorded on the sub-order at checkout, default 5%) to PLATFORM_REVENUE.

item.name: POST /orders/sub-orders/{id}/cancel - Buyer cancels a sub-order that has not shipped yet (escrow refunded, stock restored)

request.description: Buyer cancels a sub-order that has not shipped yet (escrow refunded, stock restored)

item.name: Disputes
POST /orders/sub-orders/{id}/dispute - Buyer opens a dispute on a shipped sub-order (freezes its escrow)

request.description:
Allowed while the sub-order is SHIPPED (or DELIVERED). It becomes DISPUTED: the vendor is not
paid, the buyer cannot cancel or confirm, and the auto-complete job skips it until an admin
resolves the dispute. Evidence is a list of text notes and image URLs (max 10).

item.name: GET /disputes - Disputes I am part of (as buyer or vendor); an admin sees all

request.description: Disputes I am part of (as buyer or vendor); an admin sees all

item.name: GET /disputes/{id} - One dispute (its buyer, its vendor, or an admin)

request.description: One dispute (its buyer, its vendor, or an admin)

item.name: POST /disputes/{id}/resolve - Admin resolves a dispute (full refund, partial refund or reject)

request.description:
Settles the frozen escrow in one ledger transaction and records the admin and the note.
FULL_REFUND returns everything to the buyer (sub-order REFUNDED). PARTIAL_REFUND returns
`refundKobo` to the buyer and pays the rest to the vendor, with commission on the vendor's
part only. REJECT releases everything to the vendor as a normal completion.

item.name: Payouts
POST /payouts - Vendor requests a payout to their bank account

exec: try { const v = j.data.payout.id; if (v) pm.collectionVariables.set('payoutId', v); } catch (e) {}

header.description: New value per logical request; reuse it to see the replay.

request.description:
Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. The amount (integer kobo, at least the minimum, N1,000
by default) leaves the wallet immediately for PLATFORM_PAYOUT_CLEARING; a background job
then sends it. A vendor may have only one PENDING payout at a time. If the transfer fails
the money returns to the wallet.

item.name: GET /payouts - My payouts, newest first

request.description: My payouts, newest first

item.name: GET /payouts/{id} - One payout (its owner, or an admin). The bank account number is masked.

request.description: One payout (its owner, or an admin). The bank account number is masked.

item.name: Webhooks
POST /webhooks/paystack - Paystack webhook (signature required)

request.description:
Verifies `x-paystack-signature` = HMAC SHA512 of the raw body with the secret key; anything
unsigned or wrongly signed is 401. Duplicate deliveries are acknowledged and ignored. On
`charge.success` the transaction is re-verified with Paystack before the wallet is credited.

item.name: POST /dev/mock-payments/{reference}/pay - DEV ONLY - simulate the customer paying (or failing) a mock top-up

request.description:
Exists only when PAYMENT_PROVIDER=mock and NODE_ENV is not production. Marks the mock payment
paid or failed, then delivers the signed webhook (plus `duplicates` extra copies) to the real
webhook endpoint, so the whole funding flow can be demoed without Paystack.
